previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: An elderly male with a history of prior strokes, COPD, CAD s/p CABG, and esophagitis was admitted for acute vertigo and chest pain. Initial concern for stroke was raised due to his neurological history, but MRI/MRA showed no acute infarct, with findings consistent with chronic small vessel disease. Vertigo improved with supportive care and discontinuation of trazodone, which may have contributed to dizziness. Chest pain was attributed to chronic esophagitis and resolved with continuation of PPI and sucralfate. A 3 mm right upper lobe pulmonary nodule was incidentally found on CTA, prompting recommendation for follow-up imaging in one year. The patient was discharged home with services, advised to follow up with primary care and neurology, and medication changes were discussed, including the correction of an intended lisinopril prescription due to allergy.

Brief Hospital Course:
Principle Reason for admission: 
This is a ___ year old male with multiple co-morbidities that 
include COPD, CAD, and alcoholism who presented with acute onset 
dyspnea and chest pain and was found to be intoxicated and 
febrile in the ED concerning for aspiration pneumonia. 

Brief Hospital Course: 
#Dyspnea 
Differential diagnois included acute coronary syndrome vs 
aspiration pneumonia vs COPD exacerbation. He was ruled out for 
acute coronary syndrome after no ischemic changes on EKG were 
found and negative cardiac enzymes x3. He also received an 
echocardiogram that revealed mild pulmonary hypertension without 
concern for other cardiac abnormalities. 

Concerning his COPD, he was given methylprednisone and combinebs 
x3 in the ED. After admission, his steroids were held, his home 
spiriva was held, and his flovent was increased from 110mcg BID 
to ___ BID until prednisone was started. He also began 
standing nebs Q6H and received supplemental oxygen via nasal 
cannula. In consideration for the likihood that his long 
standing, poorly treated, COPD was contributing to his symptoms, 
he was given a 5 day course of 40mg prednisone, to be completed 
___. 

Repeat CXR revealed a LLL opacity concerning for pneumonia and 
his clinical history of EtOH intake and fever was concerning for 
aspiration pneumonia. IV vancomycin and IV zosyn were started at 
admission. By day 3 of admission, the patient was afebrile for 
over 48 hours, was receiving O2 supplementation intermittently 
(which was thought to be his baseline) and was able to PO 
without issue. He began PO levofloxacin to be completed ___.

#Leukocytosis 
After a normal WBC throughout the admission, patient had a count 
of 12 around day 4 that began to trend down the following day. 
This may have been due to prednisone administration. CBC should 
be repeated in 1 week.

#Atrial Fibrillation w/ RVR
In the ED, the patient reported forgetting to administer his 
diltiazem after he was found to be in AF w/RVR. He received his 
home dose of diltiazem and had a stable heart rate during the 
rest of his admission. Anti-coagulation was not begun despite a 
CHADS2 of 4, for concern regarding his EtOH intake and fall 
risk.

#Acute Kidney Injury
In the ED, his initial creatinine was 1.8 and eventually 
stabilized to 1.2 by day 4 of admission. This was thought to be 
pre-renal given that he improved after administration of IVF and 
had a low FeNA. Etiology was likely secondary to his intoxicated 
state and presumed infection. He also had an anion gap of 23 at 
admission with a VBG of 7.32/35/37 and an elevated lactate that 
trended down after IVF.  This was also thought to be secondary 
to alcohol intoxication.  

#Hypokalemia: During his hospital stay, this patient had a drop 
in K+ to 2.9 from 3.5-4.2 at admission. He had a large watery 
bowel movement the night prior to this value and may be 
secondary to GI loss. His K+ was repleted. Repeat chem7 in 1 
week. 

#Anemia
This patient has chronic anemia with a baseline in the high ___ 
to low ___ but was found to have a Hct of 22.6 on day 2 of his 
admission. His B12, Folate, iron binding capacity, and 
transferrin levels were within normal limits, and his Ferritin 
level was high.  He had a reticulocyte count of 0.8. After 
consultation with hematology and an upward trending Hct to 29.5 
by day 4 of admission, the likely etiology was thought be 
multifactorial with regard to his chronic disease with bone 
marrow suppression, alcohol use, and acute infection. He will 
follow-up outpatient to trend these results. 

#Thrombocytopenia 
This patient has had intermittent thrombocytopenia in the past 
into ___ in ___ with an initial Plt count of 77 at admission 
that has begun to trend upwards to 132 by day 5 of admission. 
After consultation with hematology and his upward trending 
counts, the likely etiology was thought to be multifactorial 
with regard to his chronic disease with bone marrow suppression, 
alcohol use, and acute infection. He will follow-up outpatient 
to trend these results.  

#Hyponatremia
This patient had a sodium of 131 on admission that was likely 
due to poor PO intake and EtOH use. This normalized to 139 after 
IV fluids and a normal PO regiment. 

#EtOH
At admission, this patients EtOH level was 150. He reported no 
previous seizures or DTs in the past, but had completed detox on 
multiple occasions. He remained on CIWA precautions throughout 
his admission though did not require benzos, was provided 
services from social work, and received multivitamins, folate, 
and thiamine daily.

Discharge Instructions:
Dear Mr. ___, 

You were hospitalized at the ___ for difficulty breathing, 
which was likely due to Pneumonia or your COPD. 

While you were here, you were treated with two IV antibiotic 
medications to treat your pneumonia: Vancomycin and Zosyn. Also, 
you were given incentive spirometry, you intermittently received 
supplemental oxygen, and received physical therapy. Your fever 
dissipated and you confirmed that you felt to be at baseline 
regarding your breathing. You will continue to receive oral 
antibiotics for your infection, levofloxacin. Given your history 
of COPD, and the possibility that this was contributing to your 
symptoms, you were started on a 5 day course of steroids as 
well. This will occur at an outpatient nursing facility where 
you will also receive physical therapy. 

When you arrived in the ED, you had a heart arrhythmia (Atrial 
Fibrillation) after forgetting to take your diltiazem. You will 
follow up with your primary care physician and ___ pulmonologist 
(lung doctor) after you leave the hospital.  You also had an 
ultrasound of your heart which stable from the prior one.

While you were hospitalized, blood labs were obtained and you 
were found to have anemia, low platlets, and elevated liver 
enzymes. After an extensive blood workup to find the cause of 
these lab values, as well as a consultation with our Hematology 
physicians, it was decided that this was most likely due to both 
long term alcohol use and your lung infection. Your labs 
improved. You will follow these labs up with your primary care 
physician when you leave the hospital. 

You also had an elevated white blood cell count that began 
trending downward. This can be expected with prednisone use, but 
you should also follow this value up with your outpatient 
physician.

with fracture of the first sternal wire.  Degenerative changes are present in
the spine.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Confluent left lower lobe and patchy right lower lobe opacities, which may
represent aspiration pneumonia given clinical suspicion for this entity.

2.  Poorly defined peripheral right upper lobe opacity, possibly corresponding
to the site of a lung nodule on chest CTA of ___.  

Once the lower lobe opacities have cleared on followup chest radiographs,
consider a followup chest CT to assess for possible interval growth of the
right upper lobe abnormality, which could potentially represent an early focus
of lung neoplasm.
